sections.Kurzabstract: The PDI can be used with patients with chronic pain problems to determine the subjective degree of impairment in everyday life caused by the pain problem. It is based on a multidimensional concept of pain-related disability and draws on a distinction between consequences of disease and injury made by the WHO (1980), which differentiates between impairment, disability and handicap. Seven areas of life are assessed: (1) Family and home responsibilities, (2) Recreation, (3) Social activities, (4) Occupation, (5) Sex life, (6) Self-care and (7) Activities necessary for life. Reliability: Cronbach's alpha was alpha = .83-.90. Validity: The unidimensionality of the PDI was confirmed. Construct validity is supported by moderate to high correlations with the following indicators of experienced disability: (1) Down-Time: r = .40; (2) a self-developed functional rating scale for assessing specific behavioural impairments: r = .78; (3) Oswestry Low Back Pain Disability Questionnaire: r = .76. Associations were found with pain intensity (r = .23-.62), the Beck Depression Inventory (r = .26-.52) and the depression scale CES-D (r = .55). Findings in inpatient pain patients, who were assigned to three chronification stages on the basis of the Mainzer Stadienkonzept chronischer Schmerzen, also support criterion validity. Norms: Percentile ranks are available.
sections.Diagnostische Zielsetzung: The questionnaire can be used with patients with chronic pain problems to determine the subjective degree of impairment in everyday life caused by the pain problem. It is suitable for use as a research instrument as well as for routine use in clinical practice.
sections.Aufbau: The questionnaire assesses self-ratings of the extent to which people with chronic pain feel impaired in everyday life by their illness. For this purpose, seven areas of life are listed, each specified by short explanations: (1) "Familiäre und häusliche Verpflichtungen", (2) "Erholung", (3) "Soziale Aktivitäten", (4) "Beruf", (5) "Sexualleben", (6) "Selbstversorgung" and (7) "Lebensnotwendige Tätigkeiten". On 11-point rating scales, verbally anchored at the poles 0 = "keine Beeinträchtigung" and 10 = "völlige Beeinträchtigung", patients are to rate the degree of impairment typical for them. By summing all items, a total score is formed, which is interpreted as a global measure of the degree of impairment.
sections.Grundlagen und Konstruktion:
The PDI was developed specifically for patients with chronic pain - regardless of the pain location or aetiology of the pain problem. It is based on a multidimensional concept of pain-related disability and draws on a distinction between consequences of disease and injury made by the WHO (1980), which differentiates between Schädigung (impairment), Behinderung (disability) and Benachteiligung (handicap). "Pain-related disabilities", as the PDI is intended to depict them, represent a subjectively perceived impairment of the ability to perform certain behaviours and activities that are to be regarded as "normal" in the statistical sense. These disabilities in turn derive from complex interrelations between biological, psychological and social factors and can vary enormously between individuals even when organic-medical factors are held constant (i.e. independently of the degree of diagnosable organic damage) (Dillmann, Nilges, Saile & Gerbershagen, 1994). An adequate assessment of pain-related disability therefore requires obtaining diagnostic information from different, complementary data sources.
The German-language version of the PDI is a translation of the empirically proven English original version of the instrument (Pollard, 1984; Tait, Chibnall & Krause, 1990; Tait, Pollard, Margolis, Duckro & Krause, 1987). Both the format of the items and the scaling were retained, and only individual formulations were slightly adapted. In four independent studies, the German adaptation was examined with regard to its quality criteria according to classical test theory. The studies examined a sample of n = 42 patients awaiting hip surgery (27 women, 15 men, mean age M = 58.40 years; Nilges, Deuker & Kirschner, 1992) as well as three groups of inpatient or outpatient chronic pain patients:
n = 154 (77 women, 77 men, M = 44.95 years; Luka-Krausgrill, Wurmthaler & Becker, 1994)
n = 40 (25 women, 15 men, M = 47.83 years; Saile & Dieterich, 1992)
n = 82 (43 women, 39 men, M = 44.68 years; Saile & Schmitz, 1991).
Results of factor, item and scale analyses supported retaining the PDI in its existing form.
sections.Testkonzept/Auswertungszeit: Scoring takes only a few minutes.
sections.Durchführung/Altersbereiche: The instrument is suitable for adult patients with chronic pain.
sections.Durchführung/Durchführungszeit: Completion time is only a few minutes.
sections.Bewertung: The PDI is a very economical instrument and can therefore be used well in both everyday clinical practice and research; it can be used with chronic pain patients to depict pain-related disability from the patient's perspective reliably and validly. Since subjective impairments often do not correspond to the extent of organic damage, the self-ratings collected with the PDI represent a valuable complement to multiaxial pain diagnostics. It is recommended to additionally consider behavioural data and to draw on further data sources (e.g. disability rating by the partner; Dillmann et al., 1994).

Study.Instructions: Bitte geben Sie im folgenden an, wie stark Sie durch Ihre Schmerzen in den verschiedenen Bereichen Ihres Lebens beeinträchtigt sind. Das heißt: Wie sehr hindern die Schmerzen Sie daran, ein normales Leben zu führen? Kreuzen Sie bitte für jeden der sieben Lebensbereiche die Zahl an, die die für Sie typische Stärke der Behinderung durch Ihre Schmerzen beschreibt. Ein Wert von 0 bedeutet dabei überhaupt keine Behinderung, und ein Wert von 10 gibt an, daß Sie in diesem Bereich durch die Schmerzen völlig beeinträchtigt sind.

PDI01.Description: Familiäre und häusliche Verpflichtungen (dieser Bereich bezieht sich auf Tätigkeiten, die das Zuhause oder die Familie betreffen. Er umfaßt Hausarbeit und Tätigkeiten rund um das Haus bzw. die Wohnung, auch Gartenarbeiten).

PDI02.Description: Erholung (dieser Bereich umfaßt Hobbies, Sport und Freizeitaktivitäten)

PDI03.Description: Soziale Aktivitäten (dieser Bereich bezieht sich auf das Zusammensein mit Freunden und Bekannten, wie z.B. Feste, Theater - und Konzertbesuche, Essen gehen und andere soziale Aktivitäten)

PDI04.Description: Beruf (dieser Bereich bezieht sich auf Aktivitäten, die ein Teil des Berufs sind oder unmittelbar mit dem Beruf zu tun haben; gemeint ist auch Hausfrauen(männer)tätigkeit)

PDI05.Description: Sexualleben (dieser Bereich bezieht sich auf die Häufigkeit und die Qualität des Sexuallebens)

PDI06.Description: Selbstversorgung (dieser Bereich umfaßt Aktivitäten, die Selbständigkeit und Unabhängigkeit im Alltag ermöglichen, wie z.B. sich waschen und anziehen, Autofahren, ohne dabei auf fremde Hilfe angewiesen zu sein)

PDI07.Description: Lebensnotwendige Tätigkeiten (dieser Bereich bezieht sich auf absolut lebensnotwendige Tätigkeiten wie Essen, Schlafen und Atmen)
